title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, numbered '- 44 -' with the exposé number 'IX' in the header and '362' as a running page number. It appears to come from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron, semi-stabilité et monodromie'), §4. The page numbering (44 / 362) suggests this, but I have not checked it against the printed SGA 7 I. The page has evidently been filed in cote 136 among the manuscript notes, whose neighbouring pages deal with homomorphisms of divided-power 'half-simplicial' algebras.

Setting. K is the fraction field of a henselian DVR with finite residue field k, |k| = q. A_K is an abelian variety. A is the identity component of the special fibre of its Néron model. Under semistable reduction, A is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. U is the ℓ-adic Tate module (or V_ℓ) of A_K. It carries a filtration U^t ⊂ U^f ⊂ U: the 'toric' part, then the 'fixed' (inertia-invariant) part. π' is the Galois group, π_0 = Gal(k̄/k), and f_q is the Frobenius generator.

Step 1 (end of the proof of the identity (4.3.5)). Two morphisms Spec(k) → A must be compared. Since A is reduced, it suffices to check that their underlying set maps agree. Composing with f_q^A on one side and f^{-1} on the other is allowed, because both are the identity on underlying sets. The required identity then follows from (4.3.3) and (4.3.4).

Step 2. Apply (4.3.5) to the ℓ^ν-torsion points and pass to the limit over ν. The Galois action g_ℓ of a Frobenius lift on T_ℓ(A(k̄)) is then identified with T_ℓ(F), where F is the Frobenius endomorphism of A.

Step 3. The characteristic polynomial of T_ℓ(F) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ. This is shown by dévissage to two cases already used in part a) of the proof:
- the abelian-scheme case, where Weil's theorems give integrality, ℓ-independence and eigenvalues of absolute value q^{1/2};
- the torus case, where eigenvalues are q times roots of unity.

This completes 4.3.2 and 4.3.

Corollary 4.4. Let g ∈ π' map to f_q^n with n ≥ 0. Then the eigenvalues of g on the three graded pieces U^t, U^f/U^t and U/U^f are algebraic integers of absolute values q^n, q^{n/2} and 1 respectively. The text then begins a sharper statement about the two extreme pieces (roots of unity times q^n, resp. roots of unity). In modern terms these are the weights 2, 1, 0 of the monodromy filtration for semistable abelian varieties. This is the prototype of the weight-monodromy picture for abelian varieties.
errors: No mathematical error on this page; the argument is standard and complete given (4.3.3)–(4.3.5) and Weil's theorems.
Archival point: this typescript page (SGA 7 Exposé IX, p. 44) is filed inside cote 136 among unrelated manuscript notes on divided-power de Rham complexes. It appears misfiled or reused as a sheet.

ideas.what: Identification of the Galois action of a Frobenius lift on the Tate module of the special fibre with T_ℓ of the Frobenius endomorphism F, via a pointwise identity checked on underlying sets
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius vs. Galois action on Tate modules of Néron special fibres

ideas.what: Integrality and ℓ-independence of the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius by dévissage into a torus part and an abelian-variety part
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence of Frobenius characteristic polynomials for semi-abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (abelian varieties); Grothendieck SGA 7 IX (semi-abelian case)

ideas.what: Eigenvalues of absolute values q^n, q^{n/2}, 1 on the toric, abelian and character-group pieces of the Tate module of a semistable abelian variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX, Cor. 4.4; precursor of Deligne's weight-monodromy conjecture

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Corollary 4.4), apparently misfiled in the de Rham divided-power notes. Its content is published and credited; the only noteworthy fact is archival.
transcription_corrections: The superscripts transcribed as 'U^{et}' and 'U^{ef}' most likely denote the toric and fixed parts, 'U^t' and 'U^f', as in SGA 7 IX; the typewriter rendering is ambiguous.
'T_ℓ(A(k))' should presumably be read with k̄ (algebraic closure), which typewriting omits.
